extraction.name: CommonCanvas
extraction.description: CommonCanvas is a suite of open diffusion models trained on Creative-Commons-licensed (CC) images with synthetic captions, achieving comparable performance to Stable Diffusion 2 (SD2) while using significantly less training data (~70 million examples). The models are trained using a data- and compute-efficient recipe, leveraging synthetic captions generated via a transfer learning technique called 'telephoning' using BLIP-2. The dataset, CommonCatalog, consists of ~70 million CC images curated from YFCC100M, with synthetic captions generated for training.
extraction.license: Creative Commons (CC) licenses (CC-BY, CC-BY-SA, CC-BY-NC, CC-BY-NC-SA, CC-BY-ND, CC-BY-NC-ND)
extraction.creator: Aaron Gokaslan, A. Feder Cooper, Jasmine Collins, Landan Seguin, Austin Jacobson, Mihir Patel, Jonathan Frankle, Cory Stephenson, Volodymyr Kuleshov
extraction.citeAs: CommonCanvas: An Open Diffusion Model Trained with Creative-Commons Images
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset CommonCatalog was curated from the YFCC100M dataset, which consists of 100 million CC-licensed images and multimedia files. The images were re-scraped from Flickr based on YFCC100M metadata to obtain high-resolution (exceeding 4K) images suitable for text-to-image (T2I) training. The dataset was filtered to exclude images with non-derivative (ND) licenses, resulting in two subsets: CommonCatalog-C (commercial use, ~25 million images) and CommonCatalog-NC (non-commercial use, ~70 million images). Synthetic captions were generated for these images using a pre-trained BLIP-2 model, which was fine-tuned on LAION-400M but did not have direct access to the images in CommonCatalog.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: YFCC100M dataset (100 million CC-licensed images and multimedia files) and Flickr IDs linking to the original data. The images were re-scraped from Flickr to obtain high-resolution versions.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The images were center-cropped and resized to a maximum size of 512x512 pixels for captioning purposes, but retained their native resolution during diffusion model training.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were center-cropped and resized to 512x512 pixels for captioning using BLIP-2. During diffusion model training, images remained in their native resolution. The dataset was filtered to exclude images with non-derivative (ND) licenses, and synthetic captions were generated for the remaining images using BLIP-2.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Synthetic captions were generated for CC images using a pre-trained BLIP-2 model, which was fine-tuned on LAION-400M. The captions were produced by passing the images through BLIP-2, which acts as a 'lossy compression' to generate descriptive text captions. The synthetic captions were then paired with the CC images to form the CommonCatalog dataset for training the CommonCanvas models.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: BLIP-2 model (Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with frozen image encoders and large language models)
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The synthetic captions generated by BLIP-2 were qualitatively analyzed and found to be more descriptive than the original LAION-2B alt-text captions, though they exhibited reduced diversity in n-grams. The captions were used directly for training without further post-processing or analysis of disagreement.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: BLIP-2 (Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with frozen image encoders and large language models)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and models are released on GitHub (https://github.com/mosaicml/diffusion/blob/main/assets/common-canvas.md) and HuggingFace. The dataset includes commercial (CommonCatalog-C) and non-commercial (CommonCatalog-NC) subsets. The authors plan to augment CommonCatalog with Creative-Commons images from other sources in future work.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes CC-licensed images, which may contain personal or sensitive information. However, the paper does not explicitly discuss the presence or handling of such information.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper discusses copyright concerns related to web-scraped datasets like LAION and proposes CC-licensed images as an alternative to address these issues. The use of synthetic captions generated by BLIP-2 is highlighted as a method to avoid direct access to copyrighted data. The authors emphasize the importance of reproducibility and avoiding link rot by sourcing CC images with known provenance.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that synthetic captions generated by BLIP-2 exhibit reduced diversity in n-grams compared to ground-truth captions. Additionally, the models underperformed in categories like faces, general photography, and paintings, which may reflect biases in the training data or captioning process. The authors also observe that the models are less likely to generate iconic characters (e.g., Disney characters) given suggestive prompts, suggesting a potential bias against such content.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited by the scarcity of high-resolution CC images (~70 million) compared to web-scraped datasets like LAION-2B (~2 billion). The synthetic captions generated by BLIP-2 may not fully capture the nuances of human-generated captions, leading to potential performance limitations. The models underperformed in specific categories (e.g., faces, paintings) and may not generalize well to all domains. The YFCC100M dataset is also noted to be about a decade old, which may limit the relevance of the images for modern applications.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluation of text-to-image (T2I) diffusion models. The dataset and models are intended for research purposes, with potential applications in generative AI, creative tools, and educational settings. The authors emphasize the use of CC-licensed data to address copyright concerns and promote reproducibility.
